ORDER These appeal have been filed under Section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 against the common award dated 31.8.2018 in Claim Case Nos.115/2016 and 116/2016 passed by 3rd Member MACT Ratlam
are heard analogously and disposed off by this common order.
2. M.A.Nos.5330/2018 and 5332/2018 have been filed by the claimants- Bhanji and Reshambai for enhancement of the award amount.

These appeals have arisen out of the same accident dated 15.4.2016 wherein NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8864 2 MA-5330-2018 deceased Papu aged 15 years and Nilesh aged 12 years have died in the road accident.

3. Learned counsel for the appellants in both the appeals submits that relying upon on the judgment Kajal Vs. Jagdish Chand and Ors (2020) 4 SCC 413 and submits that amount awarded by the claims tribunal is on lower side.

He placed reliance on the judgments delivered by the Apex Court in the case of Amrit Paul Singh vs. Tata AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd , 2018 (7) SCC 558, the judgment passed by the Coordinate Bench of this Court in the case o f Badiya @ Baddiya & Ors. vs. Chotulal & Ors . passed in M.A.No.1532/2015 dated 14.8.2018 and in the case of Hifazat Shah & Ors. vs. Ballu Lakhan &
Ors. passed in M.A.No.3784 of 20215 dated 23.2.2026.

He also submits that looking to the number of family members, appropriate amount of compensation be awarded in the head of consortium.
With the aforesaid, it is prayed that just and proper compensation be awarded to the appellants/claimants.

4. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/Insurance Company has opposed the appeals on the ground that future prospects cannot be granted in cases where minor children were not earning anything and even the Apex Court in the case of Kajal (supra) has not considered the aforesaid point.
He further submits that the liability has rightly been not saddled on the Insurance Company as there was breached of permit.
With regard to the pay and recover he placed reliance on the judgment of the Apex Court in the case of K. Nagendra vs. The New India Insurance Co. Ltd & Ors.

entities.text: K. Nagendra vs. The New India Insurance Co. Ltd & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2025 Supreme (SC) 1872/2025 AIR (SC) 528.
Hence prays for dismissal of the appeals.

5. Heard the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties and perused the record.
6.
In the case of Kajal (supra) the Hon'ble Apex Court has considered how the income of the minor children who have met with unfortunate fate be considered for computation the award amount.

Para 20 of the aforesaid judgment is relevant which reads as under :-
"20.
Both the Courts below have held that since the girl was a young child of 12 years only notional income of Rs.15,000 p.a. can be taken into consideration.
We do not think this is a proper way of assessing the future loss of income.
This young girl after studying could have worked and would have earned much more than Rs.15,000/ per annum.
Each case has to be decided on its own evidence but taking notional income to be Rs.15,000/ per annum is not at all justified.

The appellant has placed before us material to show that the minimum wages payable to a skilled workman is Rs.4846/
per month.
In our opinion this would be the minimum amount which she would have earned on becoming a NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8864 4 MA-5330-2018 major.
Adding 40% for the future prospects, it works to be Rs.6784.40/ per month, i.e., 81,412.80 per annum.

Applying the multiplier of 18 it works out to Rs.14,65,430.40, which is rounded off to Rs.14,66,000/-"
7.
It is apparent that even in cases of minor children who are not earning any specific income should be awarded to 40% future prospects.

In catena of judgment the Apex Court has also held that even Bhanji vs Rajendra on 6 April, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/183792084/
2 in the cases where income is not proved and assessed, on guess work even those persons are entitled for future prospects to the rate which has been fixed as per the directions given in National Insurance Co. Ltd. vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors. (2017) 16 SCC 680 (para 59.3 & 59.4).

8. In view of the above the just and proper compensation comes as under:-
In M.A.No.5330/2018, the appellants are entitled to receive the compensation in below terms :-
Rs.6850 per month x 12 = Rs.82,200 + F.P. Rs.32,880 - (40% Loss of F.P.) =
Rs.1,15,080 - (deduction 1/2 P.E) = Rs.73,980 x 15 Dependency = Rs.11,09,700/-

Hence the appellants in M.A.No.5330/2018 are entitled to receive NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8864 5 MA-5330-2018 Rs.7,19,700/- as enhanced compensation in addition to the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal with the same rate of interest as awarded by the claims tribunal.
10.

Similarly in M.A.No.5332/2018, the appellants are entitled to receive the compensation in below terms :-
Rs.6850 per month x 12 = Rs.82,200 + F.P. Rs.32,880 - (40% Loss of F.P.) =
Rs.1,15,080 - (deduction 1/2 P.E) = Rs.73,980 x 15 Dependency = Rs.11,09,700/-

Hence the appellants in M.A.No.5532/2018 are entitled to receive Rs.6,59,700/-
as enhanced compensation in addition to the amount already awarded by the claims tribunal with the same rate of interest as awarded by the claims tribunal.

12. The enhanced amount in both the appeals shall require court fees as per prevailing slab on the date of filing of the appeal, which will be paid by the appellants/claimants within a period of 30 days from the date of receipt of the certified copy of this order,
In case the appellants fail to pay the requisite Court fees within a period of 30 days then beyond 30 days interest will not be payable till filing of the Court fees.

13. As far as the liability part is concerned, the Coordinate Bench of NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:8864 6 MA-5330-2018 this Court in the case of Badiya @ Baddiya & Ors. (supra), relying upon the judgment delivered by the Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Co.
Ltd. vs. Challa Bharathamma & Ors. 2004 ACJ 2094 wherein it has observed that in case of breach of permit direction to pay and recover should be passed.

entities.text:
National Insurance Co.
Ltd. vs. Challa Bharathamma & Ors. 2004 ACJ 2094
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The same view has been taken by the Apex Court in the case of K. Nagendra (supra) in para 8.

Thus the finding given by the learned claims tribunal regarding liability is not proper and is hereby set aside by holding that Insurance Co. will first pay the awarded/compensation amount to the claimants / survivors of the deceased and then recover it from the owner and driver of the offending vehicle.
14. With the aforesaid, the appeals are partly allowed and disposed off.

(BINOD KUMAR DWIVEDI) JUDGE SS/-
